column1: # Idiom drill. One row per idiom. The question is one of q1–q4, in English.
# avoidN lists other idioms in THIS set that could also answer that question.
# Distractors are chosen only from the rest of the set.

column3: not even a small detail is allowed to slip
column4: She measures the spice with a scale, not a spoon.
column6: He reread the form and corrected a comma.
column8: One stitch was slightly loose, so she pulled it out and did it again.
column10: Before the guests came, he checked every glass for a fingerprint.

column3: the result cost a great deal
column4: That diploma took her six years of night classes.
column6: We saved for the bike by skipping restaurants all winter.
column8: He got the visa after three refusals.
column10: The first tomato came from seeds we had nearly given up on.

column3: people still want it after it has run out
column4: We baked two hundred buns. The school asked for more, and the flour was gone.
column6: The clinic has the patients. It does not have the medicine.
column8: Every coat in that size sold. Three people are waiting for the next delivery.
column10: The well is low, and the village still needs water tonight.

column3: a flow of people with no gap
column4: From morning to night, visitors came through the gate without a break.
column6: Taxis kept stopping. As one left, another arrived.
column8: The trail was a line of hikers. You were never walking alone.
column10: People entered the museum in a stream that did not thin until dark.

column3: many different kinds, side by side
column4: That stall sells tea, phone cases, puppies, and violin lessons.
column6: His excuses were a new kind every day: traffic, a dream, a lost key, a holiday I had never heard of.
column8: The festival had opera, a robot show, and a contest for the largest dumpling.
column10: One menu offers noodles, pizza, sushi, and hotpot.

column3: something makes people look
column4: She walked in wearing a red coat. Every table looked up.
column6: The new statue is bright yellow. You can see it from the end of the street.
column8: His silence in a noisy meeting made people turn toward him.
column10: One lit window in the dark building drew the whole bus's attention.

column3: the outcome depends on this one thing
column4: If this player is ill, the team does not bother to start.
column6: The grant depends on her signature. Nothing else matters as much.
column8: Lose that customer and the shop loses the year.
column10: His vote is the one that decides whether the plan passes.

column3: the name matches what it actually is
column4: The quiet carriage was actually quiet.
column6: They call him a doctor, and he did name the illness in a minute.
column8: The spicy noodles were spicy. My mouth is still complaining.
column10: They call her the closer. She does finish the jobs other people leave.

column3: someone changed, so you have to respect them anew
column4: I used to laugh at his cooking. Tonight I asked him for the recipe.
column6: The shy classmate led the meeting. The rest of us sat up.
column8: I used to correct her Chinese. She just corrected mine.
column10: The shop we used to walk past is now the one we cross town for.

column3: two of their own claims cannot both be true
column4: He says he is saving money, then shows me three new coats.
column6: The sign says silence. The announcement is loud.
column8: She promised to stay home, then bought a train ticket.
column10: The report says sales fell, and also says it was their best year.

column3: the listener cannot take in what is being offered
column4: I explained the joke three times. He waited for a funny part that had already happened.
column6: She played her best piece. Her uncle talked through all of it.
column8: He read the poem aloud. Someone asked when the story would start.
column10: I described the wine. He asked whether it tasted like juice.

column3: an extra touch spoils what was already finished
column4: The soup was ready. He added sugar and ruined it.
column6: The drawing was done. A hat on the cat made it look wrong.
column8: The email was clear until the last paragraph apologized for things nobody minded.
column10: We had a deal. He added one more rule and it fell apart.

column3: one action produces two gains
column4: The walk to return the book also passed the pharmacy.
column6: She taught the song and practiced her own pronunciation at the same time.
column8: We washed the car, and the children got their water fight.
column10: He took the later train and finished the report on the way.

column3: help arrives while someone is actually in trouble
column4: The heater broke, and a neighbor brought a blanket and soup that night.
column6: Rent was due and he had nothing. His sister sent the money that afternoon.
column8: They were stranded in the rain. A stranger drove them to the station.
column10: The clinic ran out of the medicine. Another hospital sent a box the same day.

column3: one task has to come before all the others
column4: The roof is leaking. The paint can wait, and so can the party.
column6: Before the recipes and the playlist, someone has to call an ambulance.
column8: Homework and the dishes are later. The baby is crying now.
column10: The boat is taking on water. The argument about the map can stop.

column3: one remark names the real problem
column4: We talked around it for an hour. She said, "You are afraid, not busy."
column6: The essay had many comments. One sentence named the actual hole.
column8: The doctors ordered tests. The nurse said he had not slept in three days.
column10: The meeting listed ten causes. He said the budget was simply too small.

column3: the cost is greater than the gain
column4: He flew across the country to save ten yuan on a shirt.
column6: We spent all Sunday cleaning for a visit that lasted an hour.
column8: She skipped sleep for a week and then forgot the speech.
column10: They cut down the tree to stop the leaves. Now the house has no shade.

column3: the moment it suddenly becomes clear
column4: I stared at the puzzle all evening. At midnight I saw which corner mattered.
column6: She reread the message and suddenly knew who "he" was.
column8: The noise was not the fridge. It was the cat in the cupboard.
column10: He looked at the map again and saw we had been walking the wrong way.

column3: savoring something, even if it is ordinary
column4: He ate the cold noodles slowly, happy with every bite.
column6: She has heard this story before and still leans in.
column8: The manual is dull. He is on page forty and enjoying it.
column10: They watched the repair video twice and liked it both times.

column3: new cases keep appearing over time
column4: We fix one leak and another starts.
column6: Every week the app has a new bug.
column8: Rumors about the wedding keep coming. Yesterday's is already old.
column10: New cafes open on this street faster than I can learn their names.
